expectations.text: Gives the actual 9.0 route: per-product credentials (SDDC Manager /v1/tokens, VCF Operations token/acquire, NSX session, vCenter session)
expectations.evidence: 'VCF 9.0 has no single "create service account, get a PAT, use it everywhere" flow. Authentication is still per–control plane.' Then: SDDC Manager — 'its `/v1/tokens` endpoint returns an access token plus a refresh token'; Ops — 'https://ops.example.com/suite-api/api/auth/token/acquire'; NSX — 'curl -k --cert pi.crt --key pi.key'; vCenter — 'https://vc.example.com/api/session' with 'vmware-api-session-id: $SID'.

expectations.text: Gives the actual 9.0 route: per-product credentials (SDDC Manager /v1/tokens, VCF Operations token/acquire, NSX session, vCenter session)
expectations.evidence: 'VCF 9.0 is not one API... each has its own identity store, its own role model, and its own token mechanics.' SDDC Manager — 'POST https://sddc-manager.example.com/v1/tokens'; Ops — 'https://vcf-ops.example.com/suite-api/api/auth/token/acquire'; vCenter — 'vCenter has no long-lived API token equivalent; your automation authenticates and gets a session'; NSX listed as its own plane — 'NSX | `/policy/api/v1/...` | NSX local or SSO | `Auditor`'.

expectations.text: Mentions NSX principal identities as the documented service-account mechanism for NSX

expectations.evidence: No mention of 9.1. Version framing is only 'VCF 9.0 reorganised a fair amount relative to 5.x' and 'VCF 9.0 does not have a single "generate a long-lived API token" button that works across the stack' — no statement that SSO-issued API clients/tokens arrived in 9.1.

expectations.text: Does NOT walk the user through the 9.1 Fleet Management > Identity & Access > API Clients flow as if it existed in 9.0
expectations.evidence: No such navigation is given; identity creation is directed to the IdP or local accounts — 'Create a dedicated service account in your identity source — AD/LDAP, or an OIDC provider federated through the VCF Identity Broker' — and tokens come from per-component API flows.

expectations.text: Gives the actual 9.0 route: per-product credentials (SDDC Manager /v1/tokens, VCF Operations token/acquire, NSX session, vCenter session)
expectations.evidence: 'Step 3: The token flow per component' — SDDC Manager: '`POST /v1/tokens` with `{"username": "...", "password": "..."}` returns an **access token**... and a **refresh token**'; VCF Operations: 'Acquire a token against the auth endpoint using the service account plus its auth source, then send it as a bearer token'; NSX: 'Principal Identity users authenticated with a **client certificate**'; vCenter: '`POST /api/session` returns a session token bound to an idle timeout; there is no static API key.'

expectations.text: Mentions NSX principal identities as the documented service-account mechanism for NSX
expectations.evidence: '**NSX — the one genuine long-lived option.** NSX supports **Principal Identity** users authenticated with a **client certificate** instead of a password... register the PI with the Auditor role'.
